architects:loader-monteith.name: Loader Monteith
paragraphs: Loader Monteith is an architecture practice in Glasgow, Scotland, founded in 2016 by Matt Loader and Iain Monteith. It designs new houses and works on existing and historic buildings, and its own site describes an approach built around conservation, heritage work and circular design: reusing materials, recycling construction waste and designing buildings that can be taken apart.

On Formground its work is shown through {count} houses across Scotland, from new family homes on farms and hillsides to extensions of listed and conservation-area cottages and townhouses. Each house links to its project page on the practice's own site.
facts: Houses: new builds, extensions and conservation

edit.standfirst: A Glasgow practice, founded in 2016, working on new houses and on conservation and heritage buildings.

makers:byarums-bruk.name: Byarums Bruk
paragraphs: Byarums Bruk is a foundry and furniture maker in Byarum, Småland, Sweden, founded in 1947 by the Bokinge brothers. At a time when cast iron dominated, they chose to cast aluminium. In 1974 the second owner, Hans Pruth, took over with a vision of making furniture, and from the 1980s the company began developing its own models with the designer Björn Alge.

Today the range is mainly outdoor and public-space furniture: benches, tables, armchairs and sofas, plus planters, litter bins and bicycle bollards. The company says its products are made to stand outdoors in the Nordic climate, and that the material is melted down and reused when a product has served its time. It still works with outside designers.
facts: Outdoor and public-space furniture, planters, litter bins, bicycle bollards
Cast metal (aluminium named on their site)

edit.standfirst: A Småland foundry, founded in 1947, making cast outdoor furniture with named designers.

designers:hella-jongerius.name: Hella Jongerius
paragraphs: Hella Jongerius is a Dutch industrial designer who studied at the Design Academy Eindhoven. She founded Jongeriuslab in Rotterdam in 1993 and moved the studio to Berlin in 2008. The studio's own site describes her work as an open-ended research into colours, materials and textures, with finished and semi-finished products as part of a never-ending process.

It points to attention for imperfections, traces of how a piece was made and the potential of materials and techniques. On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them vases, coffee tables, lounge chairs, plates and bottles. The studio's site lists projects, exhibitions and publications.
facts: Vases, coffee tables, lounge chairs, plates, bottles (as shown on Formground)

edit.standfirst: Jongeriuslab, founded in Rotterdam in 1993 and now in Berlin, researches colour, material and texture.
